Strengthen the legal, regulatory, institutional, and information environment which protects and enables the growth in associational life and the development of independent and sustainable civil society organizations (CSOs). Build the capacity of civil society organizations to act as agents for reform and support their participation in democratic decision-making through articulating and representing their members interests, engaging in service delivery, and advocating for issues which become part of the public agenda and are reflected in public policies. Encourage the strengthening of a civic culture which supports democratic institutions and processes, active participation in political and civic life, and the civic virtues of tolerance, pluralism, compromise, trust, and respect for individual rights, including gender equality.

Support and strengthen the negotiation process and implement peace and reconciliation processes, accords and ceasefire agreements at track levels 1, 2 and 3, including support to indigenous peacebuilding efforts. For a peace/negotiations process to have a chance of success, it must entail building trust in the process, between parties, and among their constituents, with a special focus on including women. Illustrative activities include negotiation training; platform development; public opinion polling; facilitation activities; elder statesmen engagement; provision of international expert advice and knowledge; financial support to parties; multi-stakeholder dialogues; assistance with the design of peacebuilding training programs; support and maintenance of agreed verification mechanisms; support to complaint tracking mechanisms; and work with local and national government representatives to bring them closer to their constituencies.

description.narrative: Support agricultural policies, laws and regulations, and institutions that: foster adoption of improved technology; promote investment in infrastructure at all levels, and enhance the natural resource base in ways that respond to the needs of men and women producers.

Assist special populations which may be vulnerable or at-risk on a temporary or chronic basis whose needs are not addressed under emergency humanitarian assistance or other programs. These include groups such as the disabled; orphans, children and at-risk youth; victims of trafficking; victims of gender-based violence; refugees, returnees, ethnic minorities, internally displaced or other socially excluded groups; the elderly; and female heads of household. Depending on circumstances, services may intend to protect groups; mitigate adverse conditions they face, or to remove barriers to help integrate them into society. Components may include measures to increase the capacity of local service and advocacy NGOs and/or professional social workers; to establish public/private service delivery partnerships as well as family and community focused service models; to establish effective referral networks; to develop appropriate service protocols and methods for screening prospective recipients; or to improve public understanding and sensitivity to the needs of the vulnerable. While services provided should not exclude victims of trafficking in persons, programs designed specifically for this group fall under the Peace and Security Objective under the Transnational Crime Area and the Trafficking in Persons and Migrant Smuggling Element.

description.narrative: recent data estimates that more than 260 million people globally live with depression and over 280 million suffer from anxiety disorders. poverty and mental health are inextricably linked and prevalent in developing countries where a critical shortage of mental health professionals means that people living in poverty lack access to mental health care. to make mental health care more accessible in zimbabwe, an evidence-based, scalable model where government nurses and ngo staff train community health workers (chws) as lay counselors will provide cognitive behavioral therapy with a focus on problem-solving therapy (pst). these trained chwsknown as grandmothers and grandfathers screen people seeking mental health support and provide them with six sessions of pst and access to an optional peer support group.

description.narrative: (Zimbabwe): .The integrated maternal, newborn, and child health (MNCH) and family planning (FP) activity will target Manicaland province with intensive MNCH support and provide comprehensive FP services nationwide. .. ..The objectives of this activity are to:.Improve the quality of MNCH-FP services;Increase the use of MNCH-FP services among hard to reach populations;Strengthen community systems and linkages to integrated MNCH-FP services; andImprove national capacity for policy implementation..Using FY 2021 funds, the activity will:.Strengthen health worker knowledge and skills to deliver high-impact MNCH and FP interventions through training, mentorship, and supervision focused on prevention and management of obstetric and neonatal complications and disabilities; Support village health workers to expand MNCH and FP service delivery; Deliver FP services in remote areas via outreach and mobile clinics; Improve linkages between health facilities and communities, and strengthen prevention and management of obstetric and newborn complications and disabilities; Improve health center committee functionality; Increase service uptake via community dialogues; Support immunizations and the introduction of new vaccines; and Support Ministry of Health and Child Care (MOHCC) national policy formulation and implementation. Mitigate the impact of the COVID pandemic on access to and delivery of quality MNCH and FP. Support family-centered, respectful maternity care in service delivery platforms through improved caregiver communication, promoting choice of birth positions, encouraging family member support during labor and partner involvement throughout care. .This activity will improve demand for and the availability of quality MNCH-FP services in the seven districts of Manicaland Province; increase access to FP nationwide; and improve MOHCC's and the Zimbabwe National Family Planning Council's capacity for policy formulation and implementation..

title.narrative: Going the Last Mile for HIV Control

description.narrative: The new program, dubbed Going the Last Mile for HIV Control, was granted with support from the Presidents Emergency Plan for AIDS Relief through USAID and the Zimbabwean Ministry of Health and Child Care (MOHCC). The program will work closely with the MOHCC, as well as other USAID health partners and Development Objective Programs, to create and implement client-centered and evidence-based solutions to fast-track the end of the AIDS epidemic by 2030. The program will change its interventions based on the needs of each population it serves in Zimbabwe at the district-level, creating intervention packages that include pre-exposure prophylaxis, voluntary medical male circumcision and condom market development.The objective of this activity is to accelerate the HIV response for epidemic control and sustain reduction in HIV incidence in Zimbabwe.

title.narrative: Accountable Democratic Action Through Social Cohesion

description.narrative: (Zimbabwe): .The activity will support efforts to contribute to peace and social cohesion, increase the capacity of local communities to deal with past human and constitutional rights violations, reduce the risk of future violations, seek accountability for violations, empower communities to monitor and document violations, connect communities to more formal institutions such as the Zimbabwe Human Rights Commission (ZHRC) and the Zimbabwe National Peace and Reconciliation Commission (NPRC) for reporting issues and seeking solutions, and provide livelihoods opportunities to victims of violence. More specifically, the activity will:.Enhance citizen support and participation in national healing and reconciliation initiatives;Facilitate access to psychosocial counseling, medical treatment, legal representation, and protection for victims of violence and torture; andFacilitate socio-economic reintegration of victims of violence and torture into society.

description.narrative: (Zimbabwe): .A network of local organizations implements the Tuberculosis (TB) Local Organizations Network (TB-LON) activity in support of the National Tuberculosis Program (NTP). TB-LON assists the NTP to design, develop, and implement policies, strategies, and services that support the prevention of TB transmission, increase the detection of TB cases, link identified cases into care and treatment, support positive treatment outcomes, and create an enabling environment for TB control in Zimbabwe. ..With FY 2022 funds, TB-LON will provide technical assistance to the MOHCC for the following:..- Implementing national TB policies, strategies, and guidelines;- Improving TB case-finding from all sources; - Building the capacity of NTP personnel on effective program management and quality data use; - Providing TB and HIV clinical services in health facilities and in communities; - Supporting health systems and service delivery platforms for quality TB services;- Documenting the burden of multidrug-resistant TB (MDR-TB); - Implementing evidence-based diagnosis, management, and prevention interventions to control MDR-TB; and- Controlling silico-TB (co-existence of silicosis and tuberculosis)...These interventions will result in improved TB prevention, case detection, case management, and the creation of a more sustainable, enabling environment for TB control in Zimbabwe. Further, FY 2023 funds will support increased capacity for local organizations to implement TB control activities and enable greater geographic coverage, from the current eight districts to twelve....

title.narrative: Feed the Future Zimbabwe-Fostering Agribusiness for Resilient Markets (FTFZ-FARM)

description.narrative: (Zimbabwe): The Feed the Future Zimbabwe Fostering Agribusiness for Resilient Markets (FARM) activity will promote water harvesting techniques to smallholder farmers, encourage them to invest in water supply and to adopt conservation practices by constructing boreholes, deep wells, drip irrigation systems, and water basins. It will also help farmers to prepare for the La Nina season by investing in water harvesting and storage facilities. This aims at reducing the negative impact of frequent drought and prolonged dry spells on farm production and productivity. The activity will intensify private sector engagement to increase access to quality agricultural inputs, and strengthen markets for agricultural produce. It will also promote access to formal and informal finance that will enable farmers to invest in water supply and other on-farm and off-farm activities. The activity promotes the adoption of improved seed varieties to mitigate the effects of climate change, improve post-harvest handling to reduce losses; provide training on improved agricultural production and post-harvest handling practices; and business skills. It will also facilitate improved adoption of household nutrition status and hygiene. More than 60 percent of activity beneficiaries are women. Therefore, the successful implementation of activity implementations will increase women's financial contributions to their households, resulting in improving their status in their communities and contributing to reducing gender-based violence. The activity is working closely with other USAID Economic Growth and Humanitarian Assistance and Resilience activities to maximize USAID development investments by leveraging resources.

title.narrative: Zimbabwe Assistance Program In Malaria (ZAPIM) II

description.narrative: The Purpose Of The Zimbabwe Assistance Program In Malaria (ZAPIM) II Is To Provide Comprehensive Support For, And Collaborative Partnership With, The Zimbabwe Ministry Of Health And Child Care (MOHCC) And National Malaria Control Programme (NMCP) And To Support The NMCP's Established Strategy And Goals As Outlined For 2021-2025. ZAPIM II Will Contribute To Attainment Of The USAID MissionS Country Development Cooperation Strategy (CDCS), 2nd Development Objective Increased Number Of Zimbabweans Live Longer And Healthier Lives . This Activity Will Specifically Focus On Progress In Intermediate Result 2.2 Enhanced Coverage Of Malaria Control And Elimination Measures . CDCS Cross-Cutting Issues Gender, Country Ownership, Youth, And Governance Are Special Areas Of Concern To Which All Usaid Programs Should Contribute And Consider. There Are Five Principal Objectives Of ZAPIM II Envisioned By USAID To Reduce Malaria Morbidity And Mortality In Zimbabwe. These Objectives Are Defined As Having Been Successful Worldwide In Malaria Control And Elimination Guidance By The World Health Organization (WHO) And The PresidentS Malaria Initiative (PMI). Achieving These Objectives Will Require Substantial Efforts To Increase The Capacity Of The MOHCC/NMCP And Partners To Independently And Successfully Design, Implement, And Monitor Malaria Activities At National, Provincial, District, Ward And Community Levels. In Addition To The Objectives Outlined Below, Applicants To The ZAPIM II Notice Of Funding Opportunity (NOFO) Are Invited And Encouraged To Expand Upon This Package In Innovative Ways To Support Quality Performance Of The MOHCC/NMCP. ZAPIM II Objectives Objective 1: Improved Quality Of Malaria Case Management And Malaria In Pregnancy (MIP) Objective 2: Increased Mosquito Net Ownership, Access And Consistent Use Objective 3: Increased Preventative And Health-Seeking Behaviors, Including Timely, Quality Diagnosis And Treatment Of Malaria Objective 4: Increased C

Strengthen a culture of political and civic engagement by promoting greater and more effective citizen participation in governance processes at multiple levels with an eye to improved, citizen-driven development.

description.narrative: (Zimbabwe): USAID's Improving Maternal, Newborn and Child Health (MNCH) mechanism helps strengthen the capacity of the national health system to deliver quality services leading to better maternal and newborn health outcomes. With FY 2024 funds, the Mhuri/Imuli II activity will reduce institutional maternal and perinatal mortality rates by 10 percent over a five-year period in selected USG-supported facilities..The activity will:.Provide financial, logistical and operational resources to national, provincial, district and facility levels to enhance policy updates, guidelines, protocols and skills to provide good quality clinical interventions that save lives of mothers, unborn babies, and newborns..Train, improve knowledge and facilitate skills transfer to healthcare workers improving requisite skills that prevent deaths..Work with MoHCC to review the numbers, types and locations of health workers involved in MNCH service delivery and help in planning for their retention in their locations..Improve healthcare worker availability through better planning, management and reviewing how MNCH services are provided..Work with MoHCC at provincial and district levels to identify and pilot initiatives that will help improve working conditions for health workers..Strengthen knowledge and skills for the processes of ordering, maintaining, and distributing stocks of drugs, medical supplies, consumables and equipment needed in providing MNH services..Train, coach and mentor MoHCC colleagues in the collection, cleaning and analysis of commodities and equipment data ensuring the few supplies available are used efficiently..Support health district and local facilities to employ more effective and efficient methods of managing their MNCH commodities and equipment...

(Zimbabwe): USAID's Sexual Health Services (SHASHA) mechanism increases access to comprehensive, voluntary, high-quality, family planning (FP) services among poor, underserved, and hard-to-reach populations with a particular focus on adolescents, young women (AGYW), and people with disabilities (PWD) across all ten provinces.. The mechanism is guided by two main objectives:.Improve access to quality, reliable family planning counseling services and contraceptives.Develop, deliver and document innovative, targeted demand creation strategies...With FY 2024 funds, the SHASHA mechanism:.Continues to engage and empower members of parliament and, community and youth advocates to participate in national budget formulation and lobby for meaningful allocations for FP and SRH services. .Trains public health service providers including community health workers to deliver high quality, FP/SRH services including broadening nursing curricula..Strengthens the private sector role in improving choice and equitable access to high quality FP/SRH services..Engages mobile outreach teams and support private and public sector sites to provide voluntary, free, comprehensive FP counseling and contraceptive services..Enhances accountability and feedback to recipients of care through digital feedback mechanisms, a youth scorecard, and mystery clients..Employs human-centered design-based approaches to generate social and behavior change approaches needed to increase access to and demand for FP among priority populations. ..These activities increase the use of FP services among under-served and poor populations in hard-to-reach geographical locations and those with challenging socio-economic situations such as PWDs, AGYW, and religious objector communities leading to improved maternal and child health outcomes..

title.narrative: Feed the Future Zimbabwe Non-timber Forest Products (NTFP) GDA Activity

description.narrative: (Zimbabwe): The Non-Timber Forest Products (NTFP) activity is based on a Global Development Alliance (GDA) between USAID and a local private sector partner, Organic Africa Holdings. This activity aims to improve the resilience of vulnerable and marginalized communities, particularly women and youth,through increased household incomes and strengthened environmental stewardship from the commercialization of NTFPs in seven provinces. The activity will increase the supply of NTFPs that meet market requirements through targeted training of 12,000 community-based collectors and smallholder farmers; investments in primary processing equipment for raw materials; and alignment with local regulations and international certification standards of NTFPs, including organic, FairWild, Fairtrade, and Kosher. In addition, the activity will support communities to sustainably use and protect forest areas. Most beneficiaries in these regions are women. Increasing women's financial contributions to their households will improve their status in their communities and will contribute to reducing gender-based violence.

description.narrative: The lwcan award follow-on seeks to expand support the design and implementation of the local works Zimbabwe youth program. The award supports the local works youth collaborative action network (LWCAN) which is made up of the youth advisory board and a cross sectoral advisory committee. The activity will also facilitate development of a youth entrepreneurship development ecosystem and support short and long-term stakeholder plans, increase communication and collaborative action and innovation within and among stakeholder groups, and gather representatives of the ecosystem regularly (round tables, public forums, etc. ) to assess progress and plan for the future of youth entrepreneurship in Zimbabwe. "

This local works program award will seek to create employment opportunities for zaka youths as well as enhance their civic participation and access to youth-friendly health services. This activity has been co-created by USAID and tariro youth development trust.

This local works program award will seek to support youth initiatives to boost their employment and economic empowerment by identifying, nurturing and strengthening youth-owned enterprises that are scalable, innovative, inclusive, locally-driven and market-demanded in any sector of the economy. Among other interventions that advance locally led development, the activity will promote an enabling environment that allows youth to thrive in business, enable youth to acquire the skill set, knowledge and support needed to access entrepreneurship and employment opportunities and promote alignment and collaboration in the youth entrepreneurship ecosystem. USAID, prospective implementing partners and other local actors especially youth, will co-create the activity.

title.narrative: Scaling Up Prevention, Oversight, Reach and Treatment of Tuberculosis in Zimbabwe (SUPPORT-TB Activity)

description.narrative: (Zimbabwe): USAID's Scaling Up Prevention, Oversight, Reach and Treatment of Tuberculosis in Zimbabwe (SUPPORT-TB) Activity is implemented by a consortium of local organizations that supports the national TB program (NTP) to develop and implement policies, strategies, and services for TB prevention, diagnosis, care, treatment, and support, and to create an enabling environment for TB control in Zimbabwe. ..With FY 2024 funds, the activity will provide technical assistance and direct service delivery for comprehensive implementation of national TB guidelines, procedures, and other standards of practice. This support boosts health facilities to continuously improve and maintain the quality of TB services. Specifically, the mechanism will:.Assist with implementation of the national TB guidelines..Scale up of TB services to a total of 30 districts..Engage additional human resources for health (HRH) including nurses and microscopists at high volume facilities to increase TB service provision..Integrate TB screening and diagnostic services into existing outreach activities within communities that are at high risk of TB infection..Develop the capacity of existing HIV community level cadres to offer TB services..Use existing systems for tracking and tracing HIV clients to follow up on TB contacts and defaulters..Improve TB case-finding from all sources..Build the capacity of NTP personnel on effective program management and data use..Provide TB/HIV clinical services in health facilities and in communities..Support service delivery platforms to improve the quality of TB services..Document the burden of multidrug-resistant TB (MDR-TB)..Improve the management of MDR-TB..Control silico-TB among high-risk populations such as artisanal miners...These interventions will result in a sustained reduction in new TB cases, increased identification of TB infected individuals, and increased TB treatment success....

title.narrative: Emergency Intervention to increase Water, Sanitation, and Hygiene (WASH) Access in Masvingo Province

description.narrative: Awarding agency: U.S. Agency for international development cfda listing / assistance listing: 98. 001 USAID foreign assistance for programs overseas cfda narrative excerpt: the purpose of USAIDs bureau for humanitarian assistance (BHA) international disaster assistance (IDA) program is to provide life-saving humanitarian assistanceincluding food, water, shelter, emergency healthcare, and other critical aid to the worlds most vulnerable and hardest-to-reach population affected by natural, man-made and complex disaster. Bha is the lead federal coordinator for international disaster assistance, harnessing the expertise and unique capacities of other U.S. Government, non-U.S. Entities & public international organizations (PIOS) to effectively respond to natural disasters, complex crises by providing emergency and food assistance around the world. Recipient: international medical corps (IMC) this award will provide financial support to international medical corps for the implementation of a program entitled, emergency intervention to increase water, sanitation, and hygiene (WASH) access in masvingo province in Zimbabwe. The goal is to mitigate the effects of the el nio-induced poor access to safe water, inadequate sanitation and poor hygiene practices in masvingo province with the purpose(S): to prevent the outbreak of WASH related diseases through improving access to safe water, sanitation and hygiene promotion in bikita, gutu, masvingo rural, mwenezi and chivi district in masvingo province. The total number of beneficiaries that will be supported under this award is 613,039 individuals.

Awarding agency: U.S. Agency for international development cfda listing / assistance listing: 98. 001 USAID foreign assistance for programs overseas cfda narrative excerpt: the purpose of USAIDs bureau for humanitarian assistance (BHA) international disaster assistance (IDA) program is to provide life-saving humanitarian assistanceincluding food, water, shelter, emergency healthcare, and other critical aid to the worlds most vulnerable and hardest-to-reach population affected by natural, man-made and complex disaster. Bha is the lead federal coordinator for international disaster assistance, harnessing the expertise and unique capacities of other U.S. Government, non-U.S. Entities & public international organizations (PIOS) to effectively respond to natural disasters, complex crises by providing emergency and food assistance around the world. Recipient: united nations world food programme (WFP) the purpose of this award is to provide financial support to united nations world food programme (WFP) for program entitled activity 1 emergency food assistance (in-kind or cash) to food insecure people, including refugees, while supporting national institutions in delivering social and humanitarian aid in Zimbabwe. The program goal is to provide emergency food assistance to refugees at tongogara refugee camp (TRC) focused on ending hunger and ensuring access to food. This intervention falls under strategic objective one of the WFPs country strategic (July 2022- December 2026), which seeks to ensure that refugees in trc meet their basic food and nutrition needs through the provision of unconditional food assistance (in-kind food and cash). The total number of beneficiaries that will be supported under this award is 13,900 refugees.

description.narrative: Title II Development Program through World Food Program.

A five-year United States Agency for International Development (USAID) Bureau of Humanitarian Assistance (BHA) funded food security and resilience program. The program focuses on Manicaland and Masvingo provinces targeting 301,636 vulnerable and food insecure women, men, and youth (young men and women) from extremely poor and chronically vulnerable households (HHs); HHs with adolescents, children, and women at risk of chronic and acute malnutrition.

(Zimbabwe): .The Parliamentary Support Program (PSP) strives to strengthen the capacity of the Zimbabwean Parliament to effectively carry out its legislative, representative, and oversight functions more effectively. The activity enhances parliamentary oversight of the Executive and other state institutions and enables Parliament to play a more significant role in improving the lives of its citizens and to exercise more influence in the governance of the country... ..With FY 2021 funds, the activity will:.Strengthen the technical and research capacities of legislators and parliamentary staff in legislative analysis, drafting, policy analysis, reporting, and the implementation of work plans; Support the drafting and submission of two private member bills; Convene meetings between Parliament, government ministries, and civil society organizations to discuss draft bills produced by stakeholders outside Parliament; Provide technical assistance in the revision of Parliament's Standing Rules and Orders to enhance inclusion and effectiveness in parliamentary processes; Provide assistance to parliamentary caucuses, possibly including the Children's and Women's Caucuses, to enhance members' ability to more effectively contribute to the work of Parliament and assume leadership roles within the institution; and Build parliamentarians' capacity to represent their constituencies and the issues and interests of their constituents.. .

description.narrative: Assist special populations which may be vulnerable or at-risk on a temporary or chronic basis whose needs are not addressed under emergency humanitarian assistance or other programs. These include groups such as the disabled; orphans, children and at-risk youth; victims of trafficking; victims of gender-based violence; refugees, returnees, ethnic minorities, internally displaced or other socially excluded groups; the elderly; and female heads of household. Depending on circumstances, services may intend to protect groups; mitigate adverse conditions they face, or to remove barriers to help integrate them into society. Components may include measures to increase the capacity of local service and advocacy NGOs and/or professional social workers; to establish public/private service delivery partnerships as well as family and community focused service models; to establish effective referral networks; to develop appropriate service protocols and methods for screening prospective recipients; or to improve public understanding and sensitivity to the needs of the vulnerable. While services provided should not exclude victims of trafficking in persons, programs designed specifically for this group fall under the Peace and Security Objective under the Transnational Crime Area and the Trafficking in Persons and Migrant Smuggling Element.

title.narrative: Families and Communities for Elimination of Pediatric HIV (FACE-Pediatric HIV)

description.narrative: Building on the achievements from the Family AIDS Initiative (FAI), USAID awarded funding to OPHID for a five-year program, entitled, Families and Communities for Elimination of Pediatric HIV (FACE-Pediatric HIV). The FACE Pediatric HIV program is implemented by a consortium of partners who bring a wide range of technical expertise and over ten years of experience in designing, implementing and leveraging support towards Prevention of Mother to Child Transmission of HIV in Zimbabwe. The program will expand access to high-quality prevention of mother-to-child transmission of HIV (PMTCT) services that are closely linked to HIV/AIDS treatment, care, and support for families, including children living with HIV.

description.narrative: (Zimbabwe): .With FY 2016 funds, USAID/Zimbabwe's Improving Family Planning Service project will continue to train and maintain nine clinical outreach teams and a social franchise network of 50 private medical service providers to: conduct awareness campaigns and increase the population's knowledge of modern Family Planning (FP) methods and FP service availability; conduct outreach services and deliver FP methods of choice to 140,000 men and women; and provide FP social franchise services to 70,000 men and women in rural, peri-urban, and urban areas in three provinces. These services are expected to avert 114,000 unintended pregnancies and 290 maternal deaths......

title.narrative: Citizens Participation in Democratic Processes Program

description.narrative: (Zimbabwe): .The Strengthening Citizen Participation in Democratic Processes Program mobilizes citizens to engage in political processes at the local level and thereby enhance their voices in the national political dialogue. If a proposed extension for this activity is approved, FY 2016 Funds will be used to:.Strengthen the capacity of ZimRights' grassroots structures and independent community-based organizations (CBOs) to more effectively mobilize citizens to participate in democratic processes through activities including needs-based trainings and technical assistance, membership outreach, and community-led public policy forums;Sponsor youth- and women-focused town hall meetings; andIncrease citizen awareness of Zimbabwe's 2013 Constitution.

title.narrative: Strengthening Regional Advocacy on Zimbabwe's Transition Project

description.narrative: (Zimbabwe): Strengthening Regional Advocacy on Zimbabwe's Transition aims to achieve sustained broad-based dialogue on socio-political issues between Zimbabwean civil society organizations and their Southern Africa Development Community (SADC) counterparts~in order to maintain international diplomatic pressure on the Zimbabwean Government to implement reforms articulated in the new constitution and maintain a democratic trajectory.With FY~2014 funds, the activity will:-Commission at least two research projects on key democratic issues such as managing prolonged transitions to inform advocacy strategies-Sponsor at least four joint press statements between Zimbabwean and regional democratic actors-Assist regional democratic actors and organizations to conduct three fact-finding missions to Zimbabwe focusing on issues including elections, political conflict and economic instability, to better inform their lobbying efforts targeting their respective governments to act on Zimbabwe through diplomatic platforms such as SADC.-Organize at least four sectorial advocacy and network-building missions to SADC countries, focusing on women, youth, faith-based organizations and trade unions-Develop and implement a communications strategy and expand use of various platforms for information dissemination about the political and economic situation in Zimbabwe

title.narrative: Legal Services and Advocacy for Human Rights Defenders

description.narrative: (Zimbabwe): Zimbabwe Lawyers for Human Rights (ZLHR) aims to enhance the protection of human rights and contribute to the increased resiliency of communities and human rights defenders (HRDs).With FY 2015 funds, the activity will:-Provide comprehensive legal defense services to HRDs subjected to illegal arrest and torture through approximately 50 emergency response cases and 35 follow-on trials-Reduce impunity of perpetrators of political violence in Zimbabwe and assist citizens to better defend their basic rights and freedoms through approximately 55 anti-impunity claims and public interest litigation-Effectively monitor, document and disseminate information on human rights violations against HRDs-Strengthen the personal and organizational security of approximately 15 threatened civil society organizations (CSOs)Build capacity of grassroots CSOs on possible legal interventions in target communities facing political violence.

title.narrative: Zimbabwe Orphans and Other Vulnerable Children (OVC) Project

description.narrative: The overall goal of the new project is to mitigate the impact of HIV and AIDS on Zimbabwe's children by enhancing the sustainability of care and support services for OVC. This is to be accomplished by strengthening the capacity of: (1) Communities and local service providers to support vulnerable families and children (2) Vulnerable households to care for children (3) The public sector social service system to support vulnerable families and children.

Support and strengthen the negotiation process and implement peace and reconciliation processes, accords and ceasefire agreements at track levels 1, 2 and 3, including support to indigenous peacebuilding efforts. For a peace/negotiations process to have a chance of success, it must entail building trust in the process, between parties, and among their constituents, with a special focus on including women. Illustrative activities include negotiation training; platform development; public opinion polling; facilitation activities; elder statesmen engagement; provision of international expert advice and knowledge; financial support to parties; multi-stakeholder dialogues; assistance with the design of peacebuilding training programs; support and maintenance of agreed verification mechanisms; support to complaint tracking mechanisms; and work with local and national government representatives to bring them closer to their constituencies.

description.narrative: Mavambo Children Vana (MCV) program in Zimbabwe is to mitigate the impact of HIV and AIDS on OVC and their households

Children Tariro (CT) aims to mitigate the impact of HIV/AIDS on Zimbabwe's children by enhancing care and support services for orphans and vulnerable children under the National Action Plan for OVC (NAPII). The objectives of the activity are 1) Strengthen the capacity of communities and local service providers to support vulnerable families and children; 2) Strengthen the capacity of vulnerable households to care for children; 3) Strengthen the capacity of the public sector social service system to support vulnerable families and children; and 4) Strengthen the capacity of communities to support vulnerable children and their families to access prevention, care and treatment of HIV services. FACT Children Tariro OVC program employs a systemic approach which builds on Department of Child Welfare and Protection Services (DPWPS) strategy and FACTs integrated Community Care of OVC model of offering wrap around services to children and their families.

title.narrative: Feed the Future Zimbabwe – Crop Development (FTF-CD)

description.narrative: (Zimbabwe): .The five-year FTFZ-CD activity provides capacity building and technical assistance to increase incomes and food security of 28,500 smallholder agricultural producers. FTFZ-CD focuses on high-value and staple food crops to improve agricultural practices and post-harvest handling, while building business skills so that small scale family producers can move into commercial farming. ..With FY 2019 funds FTFZ-CD will:.Provide "farming as a business" and nutrition sensitive agriculture training; Link beneficiaries to financial institutions to increase access to credit for trade, production, and capital investment;Link farmers to local food processors to increase access to reliable markets;Train farmers on nutrition and hygiene behavior change; Promote women farmers in leadership roles; andAssist beneficiaries affected by Cyclone Idai to recover livelihoods lost in the cyclone..

Ensure broadly accessible, reliable and economically sustainable water and sanitation services for health, security, and prosperity. (Note that this element does not include the household behavior aspects found in sub-element 1.6.7 or water issues directly relating to Agriculture found in the EG Objective.)

description.narrative: Strengthen the legal, regulatory, institutional, and information environment which protects and enables the growth in associational life and the development of independent and sustainable civil society organizations (CSOs). Build the capacity of civil society organizations to act as agents for reform and support their participation in democratic decision-making through articulating and representing their members interests, engaging in service delivery, and advocating for issues which become part of the public agenda and are reflected in public policies. Encourage the strengthening of a civic culture which supports democratic institutions and processes, active participation in political and civic life, and the civic virtues of tolerance, pluralism, compromise, trust, and respect for individual rights, including gender equality.

description.narrative: (Zimbabwe): USAID's Zimbabwe Assistance Program in Malaria (ZAPIM) provides comprehensive malaria prevention, treatment, and support to the Ministry of Health and Child Care, National Malaria Control Program (NMCP) and partners. ZAPIM mainly operates in three provinces (Mashonaland East, Mashonaland Central, and Matabeleland North) of Zimbabwe, covering a total of 15 districts..With FY 2019 funds, ZAPIM will conduct the following activities:.Distribute long-lasting insecticidal nets (LLIN) through selected continuous distribution channels in target districts; Support supervision and training of primary health facility and/or community health staff in malaria case management, malaria in pregnancy, and malaria rapid diagnostic testing; Support the production and distribution of malaria behavior change communication materials; and Strengthen malaria surveillance, monitoring, and evaluation and ensure evidence-based programming and decision making through strengthening of program data collection, training on integrated disease surveillance and response, and conducting assessments of LLIN durability and other operational research.... .. .

title.narrative: Advancing Promotion and Protection of Human Rights through Legal Services, Rights Literacy, Training and Advocacy

description.narrative: (Zimbabwe): Advancing Promotion and Protection of Human Rights through Legal Services, Rights Literacy, Training, and Advocacy will provide essential support services to human rights defenders (HRDs) and victims of human and constitutional rights violations that will enable them to continue to assert and demand their rights and freedoms and to hold relevant state and non-state actors accountable.With FY 2019 funds, the activity will:.Provide comprehensive legal defense services to HRDs subjected to illegal arrest and torture through emergency case response and follow-on trials;Litigate public interest, strategic impact, anti-impunity, and constitutional cases to advance key constitutional reforms;Work with citizens, civil society, and other stakeholders to increase their awareness of constitutional rights, roles, and responsibilities;Monitor, document, and disseminate information on human and constitutional rights violations against HRDs; andStrengthen the personal and organizational security of threatened civil society organizations..

title.narrative: Strategic Economic Research and Analysis (SERA) Project

description.narrative: (Zimbabwe): The Strategic Economic Research and Analysis (SERA) program promotes good economic governance by improving evidence-based economic policy research, advocacy, and dialogue through work with civil society organizations, local think-tanks, and business associations to inform the public policy-making process. The program provides limited training to government economists to improve analytical capabilities, and encourage good economic governance by building their capacity to increase government transparency and accountability. With FY 2015 funds, SERA will: -Build capacity of local think-tanks, civil society organizations (CSO), and business associations to develop, analyze, and disseminate evidence-based research. -Work with CSOs to advocate for greater transparency and improved economic governance in areas such as pension and parastatal reforms, fiscal management, and anti-corruption. -Build government ministries' analytical skills to improve accountability and effectiveness of economic governance, encourage fiscal transparency, and minimize opportunities for corruption.

title.narrative: Feed the Future Zimbabwe – Livestock Development (FTF-LD)

description.narrative: (Zimbabwe): The FTFZ-LD program increases incomes and food security of smallholder agricultural producers, by building their capacity to participate in the livestock and dairy value chains. With FY 2019 funds, the program will target 3,000 smallholder livestock farmer households (1,800 beef and 1,200 dairy cattle farmers). .With FY 2019 funds, the FTFZ-LD program will:.Train farmers in good animal husbandry practices to increase productivity and production for household meat, eggs, and dairy consumption as well as marketing; Link small producers to financial institutions to increase access to credit for trade, production, and capital investment; Improve market linkages of small-scale producers with input suppliers and buyers; Train households on hygiene and nutrition;Promote women farmers in leadership roles; andDevelop the small-scale milk aggregator model to increase farmers' access to the dairy value chain.... .

title.narrative: Civic Engagement for Accountability and Democracy in Zimbabwe

description.narrative: (Zimbabwe): .The program provides grants, technical assistance, and learning support to Civil Society Organizations (CSOs) in advocacy, oversight, implementation of constitutional provisions, civil and political rights, and women and youth empowerment. ..With FY 2019 funds, the activity will support:.Advocacy and outreach to advance democratic reform and good governance;Social accountability programs at the community level for constructive dialogue and oversight; Media efforts to monitor and publicize the work of governance actors and provide platforms for citizen engagement;Technical capacity and support for women and youth organizations, community-based organizations, and citizen groups; CSO monitoring of the legislative reform and constitutional realignment process;Strategic litigation on constitutional issues and critical reforms;Community-level engagement that works with men and women to break down harmful norms and attitudes around femininity and masculinity, shift attitudes and behaviors around caregiving and other responsibilities within the home, and foster increased recognition of and openness to women's roles in civic participation and leadership; andLeadership training, mentorship programs, and networking for youth, women and civil society actors. .

title.narrative: Inclusive PPA Business model for developing underutilized plants to improve food security in Zimbabwe

description.narrative: The Business Model for Developing Underutilized Plants to Improve Food Security in Zimbabwe is a 3-year public-private partnership between an NGO (HWA - Hilfswerk Austria International Zimbabwe), a local research organization (BIZ Bio-Innovation Zimbabwe), and a private company (KAITE Pvt Ltd). The program aims to commercialize a number of indigenous plants for which significant potential market opportunities exist, and to demonstrate the opportunities that underutilized plants hold for smallholder farmers in Natural Regions 4 and 5.

title.narrative: ZIMBABWE - Household Economic Strengthening for Adolescent Girls and Young Women in DREAMS Districts Project

description.narrative: The purpose of this program is to address the disproportionately high HIV incidence rates among adolescent girls and young women and to expand the existing Harmonized Social Cash Transfer program into 4 additional districts.

Zimbabwe:Works is preparing the countrys marginalized young people to enter the workforce. With initial funding from USAID and an additional commitment from DFID and the Embassy of Sweden (Sida), this initiative has brought the International Youth Foundation into partnership with local NGOs and companies to provide critical job readiness training. The project also helps future entrepreneurs succeed in self-employment through business coursework and access to microfinance loans and savings and loan programs. Through use of locally adapted Passport to Success curriculum, the project is empowering young Zimbabweans with life skills such as increased self-esteem, and promoting civic engagement. Throughout the initiative, which is a part of the global Youth:Work framework, the project's capacity building work guides local partners to develop the business acumen to succeed and operate sustainably.

title.narrative: Maternal and Child Health Survival Program (MCSP)

description.narrative: (Tanzania): In FY 2016, MCSP field support will work to end preventable child and maternal deaths. It will help to develop national policies and guidelines for health systems strengthening, focusing on maternal and child health (MCH), HIV, tuberculosis, malaria and family planning (FP). MCSP will design the Ministry of Health's Enterprise Architecture (EA) within its eHealth Strategy to ensure that different health-related electronic information systems are interoperable. It will also develop a data warehouse to facilitate data analysis for improved evidence-based decision-making. Furthermore, MCSP will strengthen pre-service training institutions and promote the timely recruitment of competent new graduates to deliver quality MCH, HIV, malaria and FP services. With MCH funds, MCSP will support the introduction of new vaccines and strengthen Tanzania's routine immunization platform. FP funds will co-fund EA efforts and strengthen FP components of pre-service training programs....

title.narrative: Children First OVC End of Project Evaluation

description.narrative: IBTCI conducted an end of project evaluation of the Children First (CF) Initiative, a five-year, $17 million cooperative agreement between USAID and World Education International, funded under PEPFAR II. CF was USAIDs primary OVC intervention in Zimbabwe, with an end date of 31 December 2012. CF sought to mitigate the impact of HIV and AIDS in Zimbabwe by developing and improving on effective models of care and support for OVC and leveraging the experience of national and community-based organizations to increase access to quality holistic services for OVC. Over the five-year project period, CF included 22 partner organizations that provided education, health, child protection services and advocacy for OVC. IBTCI conducted an end of project evaluation which examined how well CF had responded to Mid Term Review recommendations as well as evaluation questions regarding innovative, sustainable and effective models of service delivery; quantity, quality and timeliness of results; capacity development for partners and communities; and institutionalization of models within relevant government structures.

description.narrative: (Zimbabwe): The Strengthening Private Sector Support for Health (SPSS) mechanism aims to reduce morbidity and mortality by increasing coverage of national malaria prevention and treatment interventions. With FY 2014 funds, SPSS will:-Distribute 880,000 Long-Lasting Insecticide Treated Nets (LLINs) in targeted areas. Increasing the coverage of LINNs will reduce malaria incidence and decrease related morbidity and mortality-Conduct a pilot distribution of LLINs within antenatal care (ANC) services in two districts in order to make the distribution of nets a routine part of ANC services.-Support a malaria training needs assessment and provide training and follow-up support to 1,200 primary health care workers on malaria case management. This training will reduce malaria case fatality by improving early access and treatment of malaria cases. -Support malaria behavior change communication activities to increase uptake of all malaria interventions.-Support training of health workers in monitoring and evaluation of malaria interventions.

Zimbabwe Lawyers for Human Rights (ZLHR) is a not for profit human rights organization whose core objective is to foster a culture of human rights in Zimbabwe as well as encourage the growth and strengthening of human rights at all levels of Zimbabwean society through observance of the rule of law. description.narrative: Capacity building of CCM

Through this project, EGPAF has been the primary partner in providing technical support to Zimbabwes Ministry of Health and Child Welfare (MOHCW) to increase access to comprehensive, high-quality prevention of mother-to-child transmission of HIV (PMTCT) services that are closely linked to HIV/AIDS treatment, care, and support for families, including children living with HIV. Over the five-year period, the program expanded its partnership with the MOHCW by supporting a package of district-level activities to strengthen district-level PMTCT and pediatric services nationwide towards achieving full-scale elimination of pediatric HIV and AIDS in Zimbabwe.

title.narrative: Zimbabwe Agricultural Income and Employment Development (Zim-AIED) Program

description.narrative: Zim-AIED supports the commercialization of smallholder agriculture and increases the incomes of rural households through the production of both food and cash crops and livestock. Target crops and products include maize, sugar beans, ground nuts, potatoes, paprika, banana, horticulture vegetables, and livestock.The program works in cooperation with private and public sector partners to increase smallholder productivity. In addition, it works with a wide range of domestic, regional, and international buyers to create reliable and profitable marketing systems for small-scale commercial farmers. It is also working with rural agritraders to ensure all farmers have access to competitively priced seeds and fertilizers and can sell their products at fair prices.

The project provides technical assistance that helps improve Zimbabwes agricultural competitiveness by facilitating evidenced-based dialogue between farmers and regulatory authorities in order to strengthen the business environment. The USAID program is building the capacity of farmers unions and commodity and agribusiness associations to enable them to analyze issues, conduct research, and advocate for the interests of their members to relevant government ministry and Parliamentary committees.

title.narrative: Title II - Promoting Recovery in Zimbabwe Project (PRIZE)

description.narrative: USAID/Food for Peace (FFP) awarded a cooperative agreement to Catholic Relief Services (CRS), in consortium with ACDI/VOCA and CARE, to implement a Title II emergency food assistance project. The project was designed to reduce food insecurity for vulnerable individuals in eight districts in Zimbabwe. USAID/Zimbabwes Economic Growth Office also contributed $2 million in Economic Support Funds in order to promote market linkage and value chain activities.

description.narrative: Reduce the threat or impact of violent conflict and promote the peaceful resolution of differences, mitigate violence if it has already broken out, or establish a framework for peace and reconciliation. This is done by identifying the causes of conflict and state failure; supporting early responses that address the causes and consequences of instability and conflict; and developing long lasting solutions to the problems that drive conflict. This includes support for processes and mechanisms for reconciliation and conflict mitigation no matter what the source of the conflict may be, though this may require integration with other elements.

description.narrative: Promote peaceful agreement on democratic reform, rules, and frameworks. Promote peaceful, broad-based participation in determining, defining, and negotiating changes to governing structures. Illustrative examples include promoting inclusive consensus-building processes related to peace agreements, national dialogues, referenda on key issues, and constitutional development or reform. Programs are designed to incorporate and support mechanisms that advance conflict mediation, resolution and negotiation of disputes in the context of these processes.
